BiblicalUsage: Kilay is niggardly, the churl, the stingy man. Isaiah 32:5 promises the vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful, and Isaiah 32:7 says the instruments of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Isaiah names the churl twice because stinginess is not a small fault: it devises wicked devices against the poor, and the day is coming when no one will call it generous.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
